findings.where: The full-width house-blue band right under the first screen: 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform' with a white Subscribe button (desktop-02, phone-01)
findings.fault: The page's loudest element is a second call to action, and it competes with the one personal contact. A full-bleed field of saturated blue, a large centred headline and a filled button outweigh the 'Write to me directly' box above it, so the eye goes there second and remembers it as the main ask. It talks about Mark in the third person in a marketing voice ('Get Mark's…'). It also offers a briefings subscription that the brief never mentions and that Mark is not known to run.
findings.who_objects: The bank official, who wants a person to engage and gets a newsletter pitch: it reads as salesy and as a firm's marketing funnel, the opposite of a personal advisor. The founder too, whose brief asks for one message, one quiet action and no invented offers or claims.

findings.where: The Subscribe button in the blue band (parts map p6, link to #subscribe)
findings.fault: The button looks like the page's main action, but its link goes to '#subscribe', and no subscribe form or section exists on the page. A click does nothing the visitor can see.
findings.who_objects: Any visitor who takes the strongest button at its word and clicks it. A dead primary-looking button on an advisor's site reads as an unfinished or careless site.

findings.where: Article specimen: every body paragraph, the subhead's lead-in paragraph, the three-item numbered list and the closing paragraph (desktop-04 to desktop-06, phone-03, phone-04)
findings.fault: Long reading text is centred. Each line starts at a different place, so the eye has to hunt for the next line through several paragraphs of legal argument. In the numbered list, the numbers sit at the left while their centred text drifts away from them: item 2's text starts well to the right of its '2.'. The list stops reading as a list.
findings.who_objects: The official reading Mark's article to judge his thinking: centred paragraphs are tiring and look like a greeting card, not a legal journal. Angélique too, because every article she adds inherits this setting.

findings.where: Article specimen: the 'Streamlining the PPP Process' card at the article's foot (desktop-06, phone-04, parts map p33, link to #article)
findings.fault: The card shows a download icon and the label 'PDF', but its link goes to '#article', an anchor on the same page, not a file. Nothing says why a 2026 lecture card sits at the end of a 2024 blog post: it has no 'Related' or 'Download the lecture' label. It is also the only part of the page with a tinted fill, a blue border, rounded corners and a wide soft drop shadow, so it looks like a pasted-in widget or a promotion on an otherwise flat, square-cornered page.
findings.who_objects: The official who clicks expecting Mark's lecture slides and gets nothing, and who reads the card as an ad rather than as his work. The founder, whose research names the PDF list as part of the product.

findings.where: First screen: the top bar holds only 'Mark M. Moseley' and the logo (desktop-01, phone-01, parts map p1, p2)
findings.fault: There is no navigation: no About, Work, Articles or Contact. The palette even lists 'nav links' as a use of the mist colour, but none exist. The name 'Mark M. Moseley' is not a link, though the logo beside it in the same lockup is a home link.
findings.who_objects: The official, who wants to check Mark's work, publications and background before writing to him, and finds no way into the site from the first screen. The founder, whose tile format names a nav on the first screen.

findings.where: First screen: the hero photograph (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: The direction asks for 'Mark at work': a full-bleed photograph of him speaking, with the line set over its calm side. Instead the candidate cuts out a very close head-and-shoulders and sets it on a flat slate field. The cutout has hard, slightly ragged edges around the hair and shoulders. Only the tip of a microphone hints at a lectern, so it reads as a floating headshot rather than a man at work. On the phone, the cutout ends abruptly at the shoulders just above the heading.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging whether v7's lever (Mark at work, in real light) shows up at all. It reads closer to the portrait direction. The official, too, may see a cut-out head on a flat colour as a little crude for a senior advisor.

findings.where: Style-tile section labels: 'PALETTE' (blue, tracked capitals), 'Texture' (large italic serif), 'Type pair', 'An article page' and 'Motion sketch' (small bold sans) (desktop-02 to desktop-06)
findings.fault: Labels of the same rank are set three ways. 'PALETTE' is in tracked capitals and link blue, against the page's own rules: 'never tracked capitals' and 'blue only where something can be clicked'. As blue text it also looks like a link but does nothing (parts map p7).
findings.who_objects: The founder, comparing the tile's stated system with what it does: the specimen contradicts its own type and colour notes.

findings.fault: The two photographs and their note fill only the left half of the content width. The right half stays empty, while the sections above and below use both columns, so the section looks unfinished.
findings.who_objects: The founder scanning the tile as a whole. Few others would notice.
